quantity: Whether two grouping factors are nested, crossed or partially crossed (as labelled)
method: Incidence of labels (m(b), fill rate, components)
failure_modes_and_numbers: None for the labels themselves; requires canonical IDs (L1-20)
evidence: E4 on Exam, ScotsSec, star, guImmun, InstEval

quantity: Whether a repeated inner label means the same unit (crossing, mobility) or a reused local label (nesting)
method: Identical label incidence under both truths (E1 part A); outcome-based likelihood comparison is T2 and weak
failure_modes_and_numbers: E1: when the label SD was 0.05-0.1 (residual SD 1) the true structure won in only 19.5-82.5% of replicates, with 2.5-42% ties; at SD 0.4 with 20 schools it won in 96-100%
decision: Declare id_scope; without it report 'ambiguous' and never recode

method: Rule R1: coarsest level within which treatment is constant
failure_modes_and_numbers: E2: one miscoded row in 2,000 (0.05%) made R1 wrong in 45% of school-randomised datasets, 0.5% in 99.8%; stepped-wedge always wrong; 10 mostly-singleton families: wrong 8%
decision: Declare assignment.unit; offer R1 only as a draft; a declared unit with mixed treatment is a top-severity finding

quantity: Whether assignment was randomised at all, and blocking versus chance balance
failure_modes_and_numbers: A class-level covariate chosen by teachers looks like a class-randomised arm
Continuous measures are unique by chance: Reaction in sleepstudy; in Exam every minimal key contains a score, and (school, student) has 4 duplicated pairs
decision: Declare observation.key; without it duplicates are informational only

method: Labels repeating under many outer units
failure_modes_and_numbers: Exam: 322 of 650 student labels occur in more than one school (up to 34)
decision: Raise 'probable local IDs' and ask for id_scope
